title: ASIN forms u = 2 - (1 - x) rather than 1 + x, introducing a 1-ULP sign asymmetry
statement: In Excel 16.0 build 20430, ASIN(x) rejects |x| > 1 with #NUM!, evaluates t = RN53(RN64(1 - x)), u = RN53(RN64(2 - t)), root = RN53(sqrt_x87(RN53(RN64(t * u)))), and atan_reduced(RN53(RN64(x / root))), and flushes subnormal outputs to 0. Reusing t in 2 - t instead of computing 1 + x independently makes ASIN(-x) differ from -ASIN(x) by 1 ULP on 714 paired inputs in the held-out uniform capture (e.g. x = +/-0.22748320798034022). All 21,610 full-bank ASIN rows match.
basis: Measured across 714 asymmetric signed pairs in CalcFunc-Evidence runs/w111-asin-acos-heldout2-20260929/answers-asin.json.gz (Excel 16.0 build 20430) and matched on 21,610/21,610 full-bank ASIN rows.
inferred: That the stored 2 - (1 - x) staging and x87 sqrt/atan_reduced sequence holds for all ASIN inputs beyond the 21,610 full-bank rows is inferred.
